text: [cheering]
>> Well, good evening, New Hampshire.
This has been a long campaign
against the backdrop of the chaos,
corruption, and costs coming out of
Washington.
And New Hampshire showed up today.
You
You spoke out today.
You said in a resounding voice that
America needs a course correction,
that Washington needs a new generation
at the table to fix things,
[cheering]
and that New Hampshire needs independent
leadership to stand up and get stuff
done.
[cheering]
You know, throughout throughout this
campaign, you invited me into your
homes, your community centers, and your
small businesses.
You shared with me your challenges, your
fears, and your hopes for the future.
And tonight, I am honored beyond words
to have earned your votes, to fight for
you in the United States Senate.
[cheering]
[applause]
A few minutes ago, I just got a very
gracious call from Jeanne Shaheen.
He wished us He wished us and our team
well, and I wish the same for him and
his family. And I think we all owe
Jeanne Shaheen a a big debt of gratitude
for his public service for the people of
New Hampshire.
[applause]
So tonight,
whether you're a Republican, an
independent, or a Democrat, tonight's
victory is for you because this is a
victory for team New Hampshire over the
broken status quo that is hurting all of
us just the same.
[cheering and applause]
Tonight's results
Tonight's results a wake-up call for
corporate special interests and
billionaires who have been rigging the
economy, for the cowards in Congress who
have enabled healthcare cuts, tariffs,
and war, and for the incompetent
president who can't even be bothered to
care how people are being hurt.
So tonight, voters in New Hampshire and
all across the country simply have had
enough enough and are demanding a change
in direction. And I am ready to fight
with everything I've got to deliver the
change that we need. [cheering]
So
here in New Hampshire here in New
Hampshire, we are clear-eyed about the
scale of the challenges that we face and
the hard work that it will take to move
forward. Whether it's building the
housing New Hampshire needs, expanding
access to healthcare and childcare,
saving Social Security, protecting our
planet, restoring reproductive freedom,
rooting out corruption,
or holding this administration
accountable, we don't have a moment to
waste, do we?
[cheering]
But there will, of course, be moments
that test our resolve. There will be
times when we hit roadblocks and get
frustrated with the pace of progress,
but we can never give up and we must be
committed to renewing the purpose of
American democracy and working with
persistence and urgency each and every
day.
I'll be honored to stand with the people
of New Hampshire shoulder to shoulder in
that work, and I'll work with anyone who
can deliver a better life for Granite
Staters and to and I'll stand up to
anyone who will take us back.
You know, across this state, Granite
Staters are showing the fighting spirit,
the resilience, and the determination
that we're known for, protesting against
the reckless policies coming out of
Washington, organizing against corporate
landlords buying up homes and jacking up
the rent,
opposing big data centers that harm our
communities and our well-being,
and stopping an ICE detention center
from being built in the state of New
Hampshire. [cheering]
[applause]
We're also a state we're also a state
that shows compassion, mobilizing for
our friends and neighbors, for veterans,
for folks struggling with addiction, or
families who are in need of food or
shelter. That's how we do things in the
state of New Hampshire. We step up. We
roll up our sleeves and we make it
happen. And that's the spirit I'll bring
to my work in the United States Senate
for all of you.
[cheering]
So tonight tonight we don't celebrate a
victory for any one political party. We
celebrate a victory for anyone, left,
right, or center, struggling with the
skyrocketing costs of living from gas to
groceries to housing. Anyone who's sick
of the tariffs, the endless war, the tax
breaks for big corporations paid for by
cuts to your healthcare. Anyone who's
fed up with the most corrupt president
in our history, who has failed in his
way of governing. And anyone who knows
that we can do so much better if we work
together.
So we know this was a hard-fought
victory tonight.
It was made even harder by the tens and
tens of millions of dollars that poured
into New Hampshire from Donald Trump,
Elon Musk, and corporate special
interests who are just fine
who are just fine with the way things
are going right now. They threw money,
attack ads, and outright lies at us
every day for months.
But we beat them anyway, didn't we?
[cheering]
We were never we were never the big
money campaign. We're the people
people-powered campaign. A campaign of
200,000 individual donors and not a dime
from corporate packs.
[cheering]
And we showed what happens when we stick
together, stand up for what's right, and
never lose hope even when the odds are
long.
It was 579 days ago that we gathered in
this very room, a place where we've
celebrated many victories with more to
come tonight.
And a place that has taught me
everything about serving the community
that I know and love, that has given me
so many opportunities in my life. Nearly
20 months ago I said I knew we were
living in deeply uncertain times.
But I knew something else, that Granite
Staters don't flinch. We don't give in.
We stand and fight. And that's exactly
what we did in this campaign.
[applause]
The fight we started in this room and
took to every corner of New Hampshire is
now headed to Washington to get our
state and our country on the right track
for the future.
[cheering]
And so
And so I'll end tonight by saying this.
I am so grateful for everyone in this
room and beyond who made this win
possible. I want to thank my extended
family who has always shown up for me
each and every day, to my amazing
parents who have set the best example of
public service
and hard work and giving back to the
community and unconditional love.
I want to thank the guy next to me, my
amazing husband Dan.
[cheering]
How about it?
[cheering]
All right, the wrong person was on the
ballot apparently.
But he's always been by my side. And
look, tonight win, lose or draw, I'm the
luckiest guy because I'm married to a
man that I love.
[cheering]
And despite [applause]
all the negative attacks and the lies,
it's nice to know that love and truth
prevailed tonight.
[cheering]
I want to thank my amazing campaign
staff led by our campaign manager Rachel
Petri
[cheering]
who ran the most effective campaign our
state has seen.
[cheering]
I want to thank Beth Kunnuff and all the
organizers at Organizing for New
Hampshire
for the work you did to get out the
vote.
[cheering]
You worked hard over the past year
communicating with voters on the issues
that matter and you got it done. I want
to thank to our thank our friends in
organized labor as who stood shoulder to
shoulder with us in this campaign.
[cheering] And I can't wait to
continuing to work with all of you to
build a fairer future for everyone who
calls New Hampshire home. Thank you to
all the volunteers, the folks who
chipped in, who knocked on doors, who
made phone calls, who got voters rides
to the polls, who talked to your friends
and neighbors about the stakes. I
wouldn't be standing before you giving
this speech tonight if it weren't for
the thousands of folks who have stepped
up for this campaign. Thanks for being a
part of this.
[cheering]
And I want to thank the team in my
congressional office too, led by Steven
Carlson and Carrie Thurman. [cheering]
They've
they've spent the past eight years
stepping up for Granite Staters and
meeting the needs of our constituents
and the entire district, and I just
salute them for all their hard work on
behalf of New Hampshire.
[cheering]
I want to thank my friend of the New
Hampshire delegation, the amazing
Senator Maggie Hassan for joining us
here tonight. [cheering]
It's going to be an honor to be with her
as part of the team in United States
Senate working closely together for the
people of this state.
And I want to send my best wishes to my
friend Maggie Goodlander on her victory
tonight.
[cheering and applause]
And my friend, who I think you'll be
hearing from shortly, Stephanie Shahi.
[cheering]
[applause]
Look, before I close, I just want to
recognize someone who's important to all
of us here in this room and who's made
an immeasurable difference for the
people of New Hampshire throughout her
time in public service, and that's the
great Senator Jeanne Shaheen.
[cheering]
[applause]
[cheering]
Senator Shaheen has set the standard we
should all strive for in public service,
and I couldn't be more grateful to call
her a colleague and a friend. We know
that New Hampshire is a better place
because of the work she's done
throughout her career and her impact on
education, on health care, on the
environment, the economy, and so many
other crucial issues will stand the test
of time. So know this, no one will ever
fill her shoes, but we all have got to
carry on her good work, don't we?
[cheering]
[applause]
So tonight we celebrate.
And as we celebrate, let's think about
the brighter future that we can all
build together. Let's remember what is
possible when we join with common
purpose and fight for a fairer, freer
New Hampshire. Today you all did your
part. We all did our part to put our
state and our country on a better path.
And tomorrow we've got to get to work to
fight for what's right and deliver the
solutions that are desperately needed.
So
my my my words to you tonight are thank
you and let's keep going. Let's keep
going. [cheering]
Let's keep going and fighting and
working for the people of this great
state. Thank you all for being here
tonight. I really appreciate it.
>> [music]
